implementation_notes: Go has no fixture framework: the idiom is ordinary constructor helpers such as 'func newVIPCustomer(t testing.TB) Customer' in the package's _test.go files, or an explicitly internal test-support package when several packages need the same canned objects. Struct literals, meaningful zero values and functional options replace the classic mother class - because a Go zero value usually is usable, defaults belong on the type (NewCustomer with options) and the helper is justified for multi-struct graphs and named business scenarios. Take testing.TB so helpers can fail the test on invalid setup, and call t.Helper() so the reported file:line is the caller's.
pitfalls: Helpers that call t.Fatal without t.Helper() report the helper's own line, sending readers to the wrong place.
Package-level fixture variables are shared mutable state; a test that appends to a returned slice or writes to a map field corrupts every other test, especially with t.Parallel().
A testdata directory holds fixture files, not Go code; helpers must live in _test.go files or an internal package, and a helper file without a test function is fine but dead helpers drift.
Helpers that return partially filled structs push the remaining required fields into each test, quietly recreating the duplication the mother was meant to remove.
